system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Cotiviti realized record after going-private merger, ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the company was taken private and
> deregistered, there is no post-closing public 10-K; realized-record facts within the
> fixed outcome window are traced through reputable press. This sub-dossier contains no
> information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- Cotiviti Holdings, Inc. filed a Form 15-12B, dated September 6, 2018, to terminate the
  registration of its common stock under Section 12(b) of the Securities Exchange Act. [SRC: SEC accession 0001341004-18-000534, Form 15-12B]
- No annual report (Form 10-K or 20-F) or other periodic report has been filed under CIK
  0001657197 (Cotiviti Holdings, Inc.) since its final pre-transaction 10-K, filed
  2018-02-22 for fiscal year 2017; a full listing of the registrant's SEC filings shows
  no periodic report filed in the 2021-2023 outcome window. [SRC: SEC EDGAR company filing history, https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001657197&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=100]
- The acquirer entities associated with the transaction — Verscend Holding Corp. (CIK
  1745089), Verscend Holding II Corp. (CIK 1745090), Verscend Intermediate Holding Corp.
  (CIK 1745091), and Verscend Holdings L.L.C. (CIK 1745092) — have no Form 10-K, 10-Q, or
  20-F on file with the SEC; their only EDGAR filings are Forms 3 and 4 reporting
  individual insiders' beneficial ownership (2018), not entity-level periodic financial
  reports. [SRC: SEC EDGAR company search, https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&company=verscend&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=100]
- Consequently there is no SEC-filed, audited financial-statement record for Cotiviti's
  or Verscend's business for the ~2021-2023 outcome window; the realized-record facts
  below rely on reputable press rather than primary SEC filings.

## Realized business record under private ownership (press-sourced, within the ~2021-2023 window)
- In December 2021, Bloomberg News reported (subsequently covered by Reuters) that
  Veritas Capital was exploring a sale of the health-IT company Cotiviti that could
  value it at more than $15 billion; the report stated Veritas had earlier been
  considering an initial public offering of Cotiviti but was weighing a sale instead
  amid stock-market volatility, with an official sale process potentially starting as
  early as January 2022. [SRC: https://www.medicalfinancenews.com/2021/12/10/pe-firm-veritas-weighs-sale-of-cotiviti/]
- No subsequent press report identified in this search documents a completed sale or
  IPO of Cotiviti within the 2021-2023 window; the December 2021 report describes an
  exploration of strategic alternatives, not a consummated transaction. [UNVERIFIED: whether the explored 2021-2022 sale process was completed, abandoned, or continued]

## Item noted but outside the fixed ~3-5-year window
- On May 2, 2024 (beyond the ~3-5-year window), Cotiviti announced completion of a
  recapitalization transaction in which investment funds managed by KKR and Cotiviti's
  long-standing owner Veritas Capital became co-sponsors with equal ownership stakes;
  the company's CEO, Dr. Emad Rizk, and Veritas Capital's CEO, Ramzi Musallam, issued
  statements describing "sustained, transformative growth" over the ownership period,
  and the announcement stated Cotiviti's solutions were used by more than 200 healthcare
  payers. No revenue, profit, or employee-count figures were disclosed in the release. [SRC: https://www.veritascapital.com/cotiviti-completes-recapitalization-with-kkr-and-long-standing-owner-veritas/]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because Cotiviti was taken private and deregistered its common stock in September
  2018, and because no successor entity in the transaction (Verscend Holding Corp. and
  its affiliated holding entities) has ever filed periodic financial reports with the
  SEC, there is no publicly available, audited outcome record for Cotiviti's business
  for the fixed ~2021-2023 outcome window. The only in-window public information located
  is a December 2021 press report of an explored (not completed) sale process valuing
  the company at more than $15 billion, roughly three times the 2018 take-private
  transaction value; whether that process concluded, and the company's financial
  performance across the window, is not publicly documented. Per the no-record
  provision for whole-company acquisitions, this case's outcome is coded **uncertain**:
  it is not fabricated or inferred from an acquirer's consolidated results, because no
  acquirer separately discloses this business's financial trajectory in a primary
  filing. [SRC: SEC accession 0001341004-18-000534, Form 15-12B] [SRC: https://www.medicalfinancenews.com/2021/12/10/pe-firm-veritas-weighs-sale-of-cotiviti/]

[SLICE END]
